resources.string: Diagnostic log copied. Paste it to share.
Capture diagnostics (reset on save or clear)

For HTTPS handshake failures, enable this option, save, and restart the target app. Only affects connections from the target app to the capture proxy. No CA reinstall needed. Disable to restore automatic negotiation.
Decrypt HTTPS (requires trusting the capture CA)

Capture only matching traffic in VPN mode. Empty lists allow all; entries within a list use OR, different lists use AND. Domains support *.example.com (subdomains only); paths are case-sensitive, exclude the query, and support a trailing * or re:regex (e.g. re:(?i)scan matches paths containing scan, ignoring case). Unmatched traffic is forwarded. Rules apply to new connections; saving closes active inspected connections.
Path allowlist (one per line; prefix regex with re:)
Selected applications: %1$d (0 = all; shared UIDs share capture scope)

HTTPS paths are filtered after TLS decryption. Android 7+ apps may not trust user CAs; certificate pinning and mutual TLS are unsupported. Captures HTTP/1.x and HTTPS HTTP/2 on TCP 80/443; HTTP/3 (QUIC) and other ports pass through without recording. WebSocket records the upgrade only. Keep 100 in-memory records, with 8 KiB per body; exports may contain credentials. Capture does not resume after VPN/process restart.

First export the CA certificate. In system Security settings, choose Encryption and credentials → Install a certificate → CA certificate, then select the exported file. Menu names vary by device. The target app must trust this CA. Remove the CA from system settings when it is no longer needed.
No completed requests. Start the VPN, apply capture settings, then make a new request from a matching app.
Start Clash in VPN mode before enabling capture.
